sourceLabel: Original practice questions aligned to the UPSC Anthropology optional syllabus; not official UPSC PYQs.
units: Culture, society, marriage, family and kinship
Tribal communities, development and constitutional safeguards

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Explain the scope and holistic nature of anthropology.
questions.framework: Define anthropology; outline biological, archaeological, linguistic and socio-cultural branches; show how holism connects them with an example; conclude with contemporary relevance.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Discuss the relevance of the comparative method and cultural relativism in contemporary anthropology.
questions.framework: Define both; explain comparison and contextual interpretation; illustrate with kinship or religion; discuss ethics and limits; conclude.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Describe the major anatomical adaptations associated with habitual bipedalism.
questions.framework: Define bipedalism; discuss foramen magnum, pelvis, spine, femur, foot and lower-limb changes; note trade-offs and fossil evidence.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Human evolution is a branching process rather than a linear ladder. Discuss with examples.
questions.framework: Explain common ancestry; discuss australopiths and Homo diversity, mosaic evolution and coexistence; reject ladder models.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Differentiate mitosis and meiosis and state their biological significance.
questions.framework: Compare divisions, daughter-cell number and chromosome number; connect mitosis to growth and meiosis to gametes and variation.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Explain how genes, chromosomes and environment interact in the expression of human traits.
questions.framework: Define gene, chromosome, genotype and phenotype; explain inheritance and gene regulation; discuss environmental influences and reject genetic determinism.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Explain the importance of archaeological context in reconstructing the human past.
questions.framework: Define context; discuss stratigraphy, association, provenience and taphonomy; explain loss of context and cautious interpretation.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Discuss the regional diversity of the Neolithic transition in the Indian subcontinent.
questions.framework: Define transition; compare cultivation, animal management, tools and settlements across regions; discuss continuity with foraging.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.unit: Culture, society, marriage, family and kinship
questions.prompt: Distinguish between descent, residence and alliance approaches to kinship.
questions.framework: Define each; explain group membership, post-marital residence and marriage ties; give examples; note overlap.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.unit: Culture, society, marriage, family and kinship
questions.prompt: Examine how marriage rules and kinship networks shape social relationships and exchange.
questions.framework: Explain endogamy, exogamy, alliance and reciprocity; discuss gender, property, residence and regional variation.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Explain reciprocity, redistribution and market exchange in economic anthropology.
questions.framework: Define three modes; distinguish social obligations, central pooling and price-mediated exchange; give examples.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Discuss the role of ritual and religion in social integration as well as social change.
questions.framework: Define ritual and religion; consider solidarity, identity, authority, conflict, reform and resistance; use theoretical perspectives.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Compare functionalism and structural-functionalism in anthropology.
questions.framework: Identify Malinowski and Radcliffe-Brown; compare needs and individual functions with social structure and institutions; note limitations.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Assess the contribution and limitations of structuralism and interpretive anthropology.
questions.framework: Explain Lévi-Strauss on underlying relations and Geertz on meaning; compare focus; discuss context, power and history.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Differentiate emic and etic approaches in anthropological research.
questions.framework: Define insider and analytical perspectives; show complementary use in interviews and comparison; discuss translation and reflexivity.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Discuss the ethical and methodological significance of participant observation.
questions.framework: Explain immersion, rapport, field notes and triangulation; discuss consent, privacy, power, positionality and limitations.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Explain the Hardy–Weinberg principle and its assumptions.
questions.framework: State p+q=1 and p²+2pq+q²=1; explain random mating and absence of selection, mutation, migration and drift.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Discuss the major forces shaping genetic variation in human populations.
questions.framework: Explain mutation, recombination, gene flow, drift, founder effect and selection; discuss demography; emphasise clinal variation.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Distinguish acclimatisation from genetic adaptation with examples.
questions.framework: Define within-lifetime adjustment versus population-level inherited change; give examples and distinguish timescales.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Examine the biocultural approach to human growth, nutrition and health.
questions.framework: Explain biological-social-environment interaction; discuss diet, infection, care, inequality and ecology; use life-course perspective.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Explain the demographic transition model and its limitations.
questions.framework: Describe broad mortality and fertility stages; note varied timing, migration, policy and uneven regional pathways.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Discuss the contribution of applied anthropology to development programme design and evaluation.
questions.framework: Explain participatory research, local knowledge, needs assessment and evaluation; distinguish outputs and outcomes; discuss ethics.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Outline the main archaeological features of the Harappan urban system.
questions.framework: Discuss town planning, drainage, craft production, weights, trade and regional variation; note undeciphered script.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Discuss the evidence and interpretive challenges in reconstructing Indian prehistory.
questions.framework: Cover lithics, fossils, sites, stratigraphy and dating; explain preservation, sampling and chronology limits; acknowledge debates.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Explain the concepts of varna and jati and why they should not be treated as identical.
questions.framework: Distinguish broad textual-normative schema from diverse local groups; discuss historical change, occupation, region and power.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Assess M. N. Srinivas's contribution to the study of social change in India.
questions.framework: Explain Sanskritisation, Westernisation and dominant caste; situate village studies; discuss agency and structural inequality.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: What is meant by the village as a field of anthropological study?
questions.framework: Discuss institutions, kinship, caste, economy and ritual; explain village-town-market links, migration and internal diversity.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.prompt: Critically examine the contributions of Indian village studies to understanding social change.
questions.framework: Discuss Dube and Srinivas; methods and concepts; examine historical context, power and limits of closed-village models.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.unit: Tribal communities, development and constitutional safeguards
questions.prompt: Explain the significance of the Fifth and Sixth Schedules for tribal governance.
questions.framework: Outline Scheduled Areas and tribal areas arrangements; discuss institutions, autonomy, safeguards and implementation.

questions.subject: Anthropology
questions.unit: Tribal communities, development and constitutional safeguards
questions.prompt: Critically discuss the challenges of tribal development, displacement and rehabilitation in India.
questions.framework: Discuss land and forest rights, livelihoods, consent, cultural continuity and participation; assess safeguards; propose rights-based measures.
